prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1088; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the initial loss report for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured states they were turning left on a green arrow when a vehicle proceeding straight struck the driver side of the insured vehicle. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles on file.

Entry 2: Contacted the other driver's carrier to confirm liability position. Carrier indicates their insured reports the light had turned yellow before entering the intersection. Conflicting accounts noted. Scene diagram and signal timing records requested from the municipality.

Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel. All contact to proceed through the attorney's office going forward. Attorney letter received requesting confirmation of coverage and a list of the medical payments available. Acknowledgment sent and file flagged for representation.

Entry 4: Claimant's attorney provided medical records indicating diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain following the collision. Treating physician notes reduced range of motion in the neck and lower back, with physical therapy recommended. Records routed to the bodily injury reserve review. Reserve adjustment pending supervisor approval.

Entry 5: Received updated vehicle inspection showing rear quarter panel and driver side door damage consistent with the reported impact angle. Independent appraisal assigned. Police report now on file and cites the other driver for failure to yield on a left-turn, though the citation is contested. File remains open pending liability determination and attorney demand package.
